title: A Extraction for the Border
premise: Ivo Pemberton, a hostage negotiator who once lost a subject named Mara and has been hiding in a witness-protection-adjacent life ever since, discovers the safe house he's lived in for three years is listed online with interior photos — meaning someone inside the network that trained him has found him. The listing is a message: come home, or the network sells his location to the people Mara's family still blame. To protect the fragile found family he's built — his neighbor Odile and her son Teo — Ivo must return to Frankfurt and dismantle the extraction firm that made him before markets open in 36 hours. He burns the network by turning its own negotiation protocols against it, chooses love over duty at the cost of his cover, and ends the book alive but unlisted: no protection, no lie, finally telling the truth about Mara.
about_author: Beatrix Oyelaran is a former crisis-line counselor who spent six years listening to negotiators debrief after long nights. She writes thrillers about people whose professional calm hides private ruin.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Scrolling property sites out of insomnia, Ivo finds his safe house listed with photos of his go-bag on the bed and Mara's photo face-down on the nightstand. Emotional beat: cold dread beneath practiced calm; the polished lie begins to crack.

chapters.title: Thirty-Six Hours
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. He confirms the listing was posted from inside Halcyon Extraction, the firm that trained him, and calculates the deadline: when Frankfurt opens, his location goes to auction. Beat: controlled panic; he starts packing the go-bag he swore never to use.

chapters.title: Odile's Kitchen
chapters.summary: POV Odile. His neighbor notices him leaving and forces a confession of half-truths over burnt toast; her son Teo gives Ivo a drawing 'for the road.' Beat: warmth against duty — the first time Ivo wants something more than survival.

chapters.title: The Handler's Voice
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. His old handler, Casimir, calls using negotiation openers Ivo himself taught, offering reinstatement if he comes in alone. Ivo recognizes the mirroring technique being used on him. Beat: humiliation curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Mara, Replayed
chapters.summary: POV Ivo, intercut memory. On the train to Frankfurt, flashbacks reveal the failed negotiation: Mara wasn't a hostage but an asset Ivo was ordered to abandon. Beat: guilt reframed as complicity; the failure on the board was authored by Halcyon.

chapters.title: The Open House
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. He infiltrates Halcyon through a staged viewing of a company-owned flat, trading small truths to a junior analyst who idolizes him. Beat: the negotiator becomes the subject; seduction of belonging versus knowledge of what it costs.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: POV Casimir. The handler offers Ivo Mara's file in exchange for signing back on; Ivo counter-negotiates, stalling until dawn while copying the client ledger. Beat: love against duty crystallizes — he refuses the deal mid-sentence.

chapters.title: Markets Open
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. At 8:00 a.m. Frankfurt time, Ivo broadcasts the ledger to every Halcyon client simultaneously, making the network worthless and himself the most wanted man in it. Beat: exhilarating terror; the point of no return crossed loudly.

chapters.title: The Long Concession
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Cornered on a trading-floor rooftop, Ivo negotiates his own surrender to the one honest agent pursuing him, buying passage out by giving up Casimir. Beat: climax — he wins by losing, choosing truth over the polished lie.

chapters.title: Unlisted
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Weeks later, Ivo returns to no safe house, no handler, no alias — just Odile's kitchen and Teo's drawing on the fridge. He tells them the whole truth about Mara. Beat: quiet resolution; found family as the only address left worth having.
